summary: 30 juin : EARLY RISK-OFF 6e session (VIX 17.65, S&P 7,440). US-Iran ceasefire rally (+1.18%) masks persistent regime weakness — breadth narrow, tech-driven. Ensemble ERO probability 44.6% dominant. Defensive tilt deepens: 6/10 scanner picks in utilities, staples, healthcare. Holiday-shortened week (July 4) reduces liquidity. Breakout strategy blocked. Sizing 0.75x.

risks.label: ERO 6th consecutive session — regime not flipping despite rally
risks.detail: Ensemble model shows ERO probability 44.6%, risk_on only 35.2%. Monday's S&P +1.18% bounce is tech-driven (NASDAQ +2.07%) without breadth confirmation. Safe-haven flows persist (gold $4,030, 10Y at 4.37%). Past rallies in ERO regimes have been selling opportunities. Breakout strategy blocked, sizing reduced to 0.75x.

risks.label: US-Iran ceasefire fragility — geopolitical risk persists
risks.detail: Monday's rally driven by US-Iran hostilities pause. Ceasefire historically fragile in this region. If tensions resume, oil spikes and equity sell-off likely. VIX could re-test 22-25 range. Strait of Hormuz disruption remains tail risk for energy supply chains.

risks.label: Holiday-shortened week — July 4 liquidity drain
risks.detail: Markets closed Friday July 3 (observed) for Independence Day. Reduced trading volumes Wednesday-Thursday amplify volatility. Low-liquidity environments historically produce outsized moves on thin order books. Position sizing critical.

risks.label: Crisis probability 15.4% — non-trivial tail risk
risks.detail: Ensemble model's crisis state at 15.4%, up from sub-10% in May. Not actionable alone but indicates growing fragility. Combined with ERO dominance, the regime could deteriorate rapidly on any shock (Iran escalation, macro miss, earnings disappointment).

risks.label: Correlation risk — AEP/AEE and FCX/BHP pairs flagged
risks.detail: OptimizeSizing rejected AEP (0.78 corr with AEE) and FCX (0.78 corr with BHP). High pairwise correlations in a defensive-heavy portfolio suggest sector crowding. Utilities and materials sectors showing herd behavior that amplifies drawdowns during sector rotation.

risks.label: No ETFs in scan — individual stock risk higher
risks.detail: DSL screeners did not surface ETF candidates this session. All 10 positions are individual stocks, which carry higher idiosyncratic risk than ETFs. Missing the diversification benefit of broad-based exposure.

events.label: S&P 500 bounces +1.18% on US-Iran ceasefire
events.detail: S&P 7,440 (+1.18%), NASDAQ +2.07%, Dow +0.59% (new record). Rally driven by geopolitical de-escalation, not fundamental improvement. Tech led (NASDAQ outperformance) while breadth lagged. VIX fell to 17.65 from recent highs. Regime remains ERO despite the bounce.

events.label: VIX normalizing at 17.65 — still above pre-ERO levels
events.detail: VIX dropped 4.2% to 17.65, below 20 threshold but above the 14-15 range seen in May's risk-on phase. The elevated floor reflects lingering uncertainty. A return below 15 would signal genuine regime shift; above 20 confirms ERO persistence.

events.label: Gold holds $4,030 — safe-haven bid intact
events.detail: Gold at $4,030 despite equity rally, indicating safe-haven demand persists. Central bank buying continues. WTI crude at $70.42, relatively stable. The gold-equity divergence (both up) is unsustainable — one side must resolve.

events.label: 10Y Treasury yield at 4.37% — bond market cautious
events.detail: 10Y yield at 4.37%, in the middle of its recent range. Bond market not confirming the equity rally's optimism. The 2s10s curve remains inverted, a persistent recession warning. Fed policy uncertainty under Warsh keeps yields elevated.

opportunities.label: AEE — Utilities momentum with 2.4% dividend yield
opportunities.detail: Ameren Corp (AEE), score 100. Regulated utility with RSI 59.8, above all moving averages. Momentum strategy in ERO regime = defensive growth. Entry $114.59, stop $110.58, TP1 $123.01. Dividend yield 2.4% provides downside cushion. Top pick in the scan.

opportunities.label: BHP — Global materials pullback at PE 14.8x
opportunities.detail: BHP Group (BHP), score 100. World's largest diversified miner at a pullback entry. PE 14.8x below historical average. Iron ore and copper exposure benefits from China stimulus. Entry $81.74, stop $77.71, TP1 $90.20. APAC diversification.

opportunities.label: NVS — EU healthcare anchor with strongest momentum
opportunities.detail: Novartis (NVS), score 100. RSI 63.7 strongest in the scan. Healthcare sector defensive in ERO. Entry $157.59, stop $152.07, TP1 $169.18. EU geographic diversification. Pharma pipeline provides fundamental upside beyond technical setup.

opportunities.label: GM — Deep value at PE 5.5x with pullback entry
opportunities.detail: General Motors (GM), score 98. PE 5.5x is extreme value for a major automaker. Pullback strategy provides better risk/reward than chasing. Entry $77.34, stop $73.29, TP1 $85.84. US consumer sector exposure.

opportunities.label: Global staples trifecta — BUD, KOF, MDLZ
opportunities.detail: Three consumer staples across 3 continents: BUD (EU beer, score 100), KOF (LatAm Coca-Cola bottler, score 100), MDLZ (US snacks, score 100). Recession-resistant sector in ERO regime. Geographic diversification within defensive positioning.

regime_blips.label: EARLY RISK-OFF — 6th session, rally is noise
regime_blips.detail: Ensemble ERO at 44.6%, risk_on 35.2%, crisis 15.4%. The S&P bounce does not flip the regime because breadth is narrow (tech-led), safe havens hold (gold $4,030), and bond yields stay elevated (4.37%). Scanner correctly blocks breakouts and reduces sizing to 0.75x. Defensive tilt: 6/10 picks in utilities/staples/healthcare.

regime_blips.label: Breakout blocked — ERO > 0.40 threshold active
regime_blips.detail: Scanner-lessons rule breakout-early-risk-off-block activated: ERO probability 44.6% > 0.40 threshold means zero breakout allocations. This is the strictest constraint in the current regime. Only Momentum, Pullback, and Pre-Squeeze strategies eligible.

regime_blips.label: Defensive tilt deepens — healthcare/staples/utilities dominate
regime_blips.detail: Healthcare-defensive-ero-tilt rule requires min 3/10 picks in HC/Staples/Utilities when ERO > 0.40. Actual allocation: 6/10 defensive sectors. The scanner is heavily skewing toward recession-resistant names. If regime flips to risk-on, these picks will underperform growth/tech.

regime_blips.label: Sizing multiplier 0.75x — capital preservation mode
regime_blips.detail: ERO regime triggers 0.75x position sizing across all 10 picks. Combined with H15 horizon (vs H10 in risk-on), the scanner is trading more cautiously. Max portfolio risk reduced proportionally. This is the correct defensive posture but limits upside capture.

regime_blips.label: APAC exposure via BHP and IX — diversification beyond US/EU
regime_blips.detail: Two APAC picks (BHP Australia, IX Hong Kong) provide geographic diversification. BHP tracks China commodity demand, IX captures HK/Asia tech services. Both are value plays (PE 14.8x and 3.3x respectively) that benefit from different macro drivers than US/EU holdings.
